Class Psram

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.Psram
public final class Psram extends Object
Explicit access to the board's external pseudo-static RAM (PSRAM).

PSRAM is an off-heap byte store. A successful allocate(int) returns a positive opaque handle, not a native address and not a Java object. The caller owns the handle and must call release(int) exactly once when the payload is no longer needed. The garbage collector does not scan or reclaim the payload.

Buffers are zero-initialized, at least four-byte aligned and byte-addressable. Generic buffers are CPU-accessible only; they are not an implicit DMA or interrupt-safe allocation. On dual-core ESP32 boards Juno serializes each intrinsic call across carriers, including registry mutation and payload copies; callers still need higher-level synchronization when several calls form one logical transaction. The runtime never falls back to internal SRAM.
